steps.tx: An idiopathic inflammatory myopathy characterized by immune-mediated microangiopathy and pathognomonic cutaneous eruptions defines **dermatomyositis**. Humoral complement-mediated attack targets endomysial capillary endothelial cells, where assembly of the membrane attack complex (C5b-9) induces endothelial swelling, capillary necrosis, and ischaemic perifascicular muscle atrophy. Symmetrical proximal muscle weakness involves the shoulder and pelvic girdles, making rising from a chair or combing hair difficult. Concurrently, distinctive cutaneous rashes develop, which can precede or accompany muscle weakness, carrying a heightened risk of occult visceral adenocarcinoma.
steps.say: An idiopathic inflammatory myopathy characterized by immune-mediated microangiopathy and pathognomonic cutaneous eruptions defines dermatomyositis. Complement-mediated attack targets endomysial capillary endothelium, where membrane attack complex assembly causes capillary loss and perifascicular muscle atrophy. Symmetrical proximal muscle weakness involves shoulder and hip girdles. Concurrently, distinctive cutaneous eruptions develop, which carry an elevated risk of occult internal malignancy.

vis.caption: Characteristic violaceous periorbital heliotrope erythema with soft-tissue oedema in dermatomyositis. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Cutaneous hallmarks of dermatomyositis display striking diagnostic specificity on physical examination. The pathognomonic **gottron papules** present as violaceous, flat-topped, slightly scaly papules located symmetrically over the dorsal surfaces of the metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints. Concurrently, a violaceous heliotrope rash manifests as a purplish erythema of the upper eyelids, often accompanied by periorbital oedema. Other characteristic cutaneous signs include the shawl sign (erythema over upper back and shoulders), V-sign (erythema across anterior neck and chest), and mechanic's hands (hyperkeratotic fissuring along lateral aspects of the digits).
steps.say: Cutaneous hallmarks of dermatomyositis display striking diagnostic specificity on physical examination. The pathognomonic gottron papules present as violaceous flat-topped papules located symmetrically over the knuckles. Concurrently, a violaceous heliotrope rash manifests as a purplish erythema across the upper eyelids with periorbital oedema. Other characteristic signs include the shawl sign across the upper back, V-sign on the chest, and mechanic's hands with lateral digital fissures.

vis.alt: Clinical photograph showing violaceous erythematous Gottron papules over dorsal interphalangeal knuckles.
vis.caption: Pathognomonic violaceous Gottron papules distributed over the dorsal metacarpophalangeal joints. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: An idiopathic inflammatory myopathy characterized by direct T-cell mediated cytotoxicity against skeletal muscle fibres defines **polymyositis**. Unlike dermatomyositis, polymyositis features clonal autoreactive CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes and macrophages that directly invade non-necrotic muscle fibres expressing MHC class I molecules. Histopathology demonstrates diffuse endomysial lymphocytic infiltrates without perifascicular atrophy. Patients present insidiously with painless, symmetrical proximal muscle weakness, marked elevation of serum creatine kinase (often 10 to 50 times normal), and an absence of cutaneous rashes. Electromyography demonstrates early recruitment of short, small-amplitude polyphasic motor unit potentials.
steps.say: An idiopathic inflammatory myopathy characterized by direct T-cell mediated cytotoxicity against skeletal muscle fibres defines polymyositis. Unlike dermatomyositis, polymyositis features CD8 cytotoxic T lymphocytes that directly invade non-necrotic muscle fibres expressing MHC class I. Histopathology demonstrates diffuse endomysial lymphocytic infiltrates without skin rashes. Patients present with symmetrical proximal muscle weakness and marked creatine kinase elevations.

points: Cutaneous signs: Gottron papules, Heliotrope rash
Strong association with internal malignancy (ovary, lung)

right.title: Polymyositis

steps.tx: Myositis-specific autoantibodies define distinct clinical syndromes and organ involvements in inflammatory myopathies. The most prevalent myositis-specific antibody is **anti-jo-1**, an autoantibody directed against histidyl-tRNA synthetase, present in twenty to thirty percent of patients. Anti-Jo-1 characterizes the anti-synthetase syndrome, clinically recognized by the constellation of inflammatory myopathy, rapid progressive interstitial lung disease, non-erosive inflammatory arthritis, mechanic's hands, and Raynaud phenomenon. Recognizing this syndrome is critical, because progressive interstitial pulmonary fibrosis represents the leading cause of morbidity and mortality.
steps.say: Myositis-specific autoantibodies define distinct clinical syndromes and organ involvements in inflammatory myopathies. The most prevalent myositis-specific antibody is anti-Jo-1, targeting histidyl-tRNA synthetase. Anti-Jo-1 characterizes the anti-synthetase syndrome, featuring inflammatory myopathy, progressive interstitial lung disease, non-erosive arthritis, mechanic's hands, and Raynaud phenomenon. Recognizing this syndrome is critical, because pulmonary fibrosis represents the primary cause of mortality.

Acute necrotizing myopathy, severe dysphagia, steroid-refractory

steps.tx: An overlapping connective tissue disorder exhibiting combined clinical features of systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, and polymyositis characterizes **mixed connective tissue disease** (MCTD). First described by Sharp, patients present with Raynaud phenomenon, diffuse swollen puffy fingers, inflammatory synovitis, proximal muscle weakness, and esophageal dysmotility. Strikingly, life-threatening renal glomerulonephritis and severe central nervous system lupus are uncommon. Long-term surveillance is critical because progressive precapillary pulmonary arterial hypertension represents the leading cause of disease-related mortality in MCTD.
steps.say: An overlapping connective tissue disorder exhibiting combined clinical features of systemic lupus, systemic sclerosis, and polymyositis characterizes mixed connective tissue disease. Patients present with Raynaud phenomenon, diffuse swollen puffy fingers, inflammatory arthritis, proximal muscle weakness, and esophageal dysmotility. Severe renal and brain involvement are uncommon. Long-term surveillance is critical because pulmonary arterial hypertension represents the primary cause of mortality in MCTD.

vis.caption: Overlap triad of systemic lupus, scleroderma, and polymyositis features defining mixed connective tissue disease. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The absolute sine qua non serological biomarker required for diagnosing mixed connective tissue disease is the presence of high-titre autoantibodies against nuclear ribonucleoproteins. Demonstrating circulating **anti-u1 rnp** antibodies in high titre (frequently exceeding 1:1,000 on indirect immunofluorescence or line blot) is mandatory for diagnosis under Alarcón-Segovia and Kasukawa diagnostic criteria. Furthermore, antibodies specific for systemic lupus (anti-dsDNA, anti-Smith) and scleroderma (anti-Scl-70) must be absent; if present, the patient is classified as having an overlap syndrome rather than classic mixed connective tissue disease.
steps.say: The absolute serological biomarker required for diagnosing mixed connective tissue disease is the presence of high-titre autoantibodies against nuclear ribonucleoproteins. Demonstrating circulating anti-U1 RNP antibodies in high titre is mandatory for diagnosis. Furthermore, antibodies specific for systemic lupus like anti-dsDNA and anti-Smith, alongside scleroderma-specific anti-Scl-70, must be absent; their presence defines an overlap syndrome rather than mixed connective tissue disease.

left.title: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease (MCTD)
points: High-titre anti-U1 RNP antibodies strictly mandatory
Leading cause of death: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension

right.title: Overlap Syndrome
points: Concurrently meets criteria for two distinct CTDs
More severe renal and systemic involvement

steps.tx: Adult-onset dermatomyositis carries a pronounced paraneoplastic association mandating comprehensive age-appropriate malignancy screening upon initial presentation. Approximately fifteen to thirty percent of adult dermatomyositis cases represent a **paraneoplastic syndrome**, most frequently associated with adenocarcinomas of the ovary, lung, pancreas, stomach, colon, and breast, alongside non-Hodgkin lymphomas. Patients harbouring anti-TIF1-gamma or anti-NXP-2 autoantibodies exhibit an exceptionally elevated five-fold risk of underlying malignancy. Screening mandates thorough pelvic examination with transvaginal ultrasound and CA-125 in women, contrast CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, and age-appropriate endoscopy.
steps.say: Adult-onset dermatomyositis carries a pronounced paraneoplastic association mandating comprehensive age-appropriate malignancy screening upon initial presentation. Up to thirty percent of adult dermatomyositis cases represent a paraneoplastic syndrome, most frequently associated with cancers of the ovary, lung, pancreas, and gastrointestinal tract. Patients harbouring anti-TIF1-gamma autoantibodies exhibit an elevated risk. Screening requires pelvic ultrasound, thoracoabdominal CT, and age-appropriate endoscopy.

steps.tx: First-line therapeutic management for active inflammatory myositis relies on high-dose systemic corticosteroids paired with early steroid-sparing immunosuppressive agents. Administering oral **prednisone** at one milligram per kilogram daily (or intravenous pulse methylprednisolone for severe dysphagia or rapidly progressive weakness) produces clinical improvement and serum creatine kinase decline within two to four weeks. Early addition of steroid-sparing immunosuppressants such as methotrexate or azathioprine is essential to facilitate steroid tapering and prevent steroid-induced myopathy. Intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) provides outstanding efficacy in refractory dermatomyositis with dysphagia.
